/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 21 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2841 (50)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4552 (123)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2103 (15)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1640 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 874 (3)
CAPESIZE
The market closed the week on a positive note, with the BCI 5TC rising by $1,118 to $41,288. Gains on C5 and C3 provided support, with the C5 index advancing by $0.770 to $14.585 and C3 edging up by $0.177 to $35.782. In the Pacific, sentiment improved as the week drew to a close, supported by a combination of miner and operator-controlled cargoes. Fixture were somewhat mixed, with offers ranging from the upper $14s to around $15.00. The sole miner in the market was reported to be bidding $13.55 early in the afternoon, while operators appeared willing to pay a premium, with bids discussed between $14.50 and $14.75. Despite the lower initial miner indication, reports suggested several vessels were ultimately fixed at around $14.20, underpinning a positive tone heading into the weekend. Meanwhile, the Atlantic ended the week on a more subdued note, although underlying market fundamentals remained supportive. Activity from South Brazil and West Africa to China was steady, with C3 bids reportedly in the mid to upper $35s against owner expectations closer to $36.00. While the bid-offer spread limited momentum, the market continued to appear well supported overall.
PANAMAX
The week finished on a slightly more positive note, with all routes showing gains, albeit minor in most cases. The P5TC average rose $138 to conclude the week at $18,928. With most activity at the start of the day, there appeared to be split opinions regarding the transatlantic market with some suggesting it was under pressure, whilst others claimed to be trading at significantly higher levels. Certainly increased grain demand from the US Gulf coupled with more minerals stems from US East Coast looked positive for the fronthaul market, so it remains to be seen next week if details emerge of higher transatlantic trades. After a busy week in the South there were fewer reports today, but the index is now above $20,000, with most brokers suggesting Charterers would need to pay well above this to find cover now. In the Pacific NoPac grain demand increased with Owners holding for a premium for the longer duration, whilst recent trades for Australian minerals showed improvements, suggesting Owners are right to hold on.
SUPRAMAX
A typically slower day with the weekend upon us, apart from the South Atlantic rates softened elsewhere in the Atlantic with the US Gulf transatlantic rate the hardest hit. There were no details of concluded trades, however several brokers suggested that the trip Skaw-Passero was now $29,000, whilst the fronthaul remained excess of $30,000. With no rumours circulating from the Continent or Mediterranean it appeared that Owners decided to wait for a new week, whilst rates in the South continued to nudge up, despite ballasters keeping a cap on possible gains. In Asia the North remained flat, although this morning the Jin Chao (63,469 2014) prompt in Mizushima was said to be on subjects for a NoPac round at either $21,500 or $22,000 with Norden, but later failed and there was talk of another Ultramax fixed from CJK at $18,750 on the same route. Recent increased trade from Indonesia has now translated into improved rate levels and the Indian Ocean continued its positive sentiment with the Kiran Caribbean (63,389 2015) fixed to Panocean at $24,000 plus $240,000 ballast bonus for Richards Bay/Pakistan. The 11TC average was up $30 to finish the week at $20,728, whilst the BSI was 1,640 (up 3).
HANDYSIZE
The market saw a typically quiet Friday, with sentiment remaining largely positional across most regions. The BHSI edged up by 3 points to 874, while the 7TC average gained $59 to close at $15,729. In the Continent and Mediterranean, little fresh information surfaced and rates held close to recent levels. The US Gulf also remained subdued, with the market maintaining a steady tone. By contrast, the South Atlantic continued to show strength, as more enquiry for September and forward dates lent support to sentiment. Across Asia fixing activity was light, but the underlying tone remained firm, with Operators still willing to take vessels. The Lolita (40,038 2024) open Malaysia was reported fixed for an Australia round in the $19,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Panama Canal Capacity Cuts

The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announced daily booking capacity limits for the second and third time this year, citing a rainfall deficit, newswires report. Daily slots will be limited to to nine Neopanamax and twenty-five Panamax from 4 September, before further declining to nine Neopanamax and twenty-three Panamax slots by 15 September. Meanwhile, previously announced draft restrictions have been pushed back, with the 14.6m maximum draft at Neopanamax locks postponed from 26 August to 2 September, and the subsequent cut to 14.5m moved from 3 September to 1 October.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve moved higher through the session today. Aug traded between 39,200–39,750 in relatively large clip sizes. Sep was again the main focus, trading between 40,700–42,750. Early activity was concentrated around 41,000–42,000, before the market strengthened steadily through the day to 42,500–42,750 in the afternoon. October traded between 42,250–43,750, following the same firmer trend and reaching its highs late in the session. The Sep v Oct spread was trading sideways today at -1250 early on, then slowly narrowed up to a high of -1000. Q4 26 traded between 40,700–42,000, with strong activity around 41,500 before firming to 42,000. The Nov v Dec spread widened and strengthened up to 2000 late on. Q1 27 traded between 27,650–28,750, while Q2 27 reached 34,500. The deferred contracts continue to make significant gains. Cal 27 traded between 32,200–32,450 and Cal 28 between 27,900–28,000.

PMX
The PMX market was supported today. September was again the main focus, trading between 20,750–21,300. Early prints were concentrated around 20,750–21,000 before the market firmed steadily through the afternoon to 21,250–21,300. October traded between 21,950–22,500, with strong activity around 22,100–22,250 before pushing higher late in the session.
